Adefoworola “Tope” Tokan-Lawal is a dual-qualified lawyer with over 12 years of experience practising law in Nigeria and the United States. She is a partner at Osuntuyi & Tokan-Lawal Law (OTL Law), where she specialises in arbitration, litigation, corporate/commercial law, copyright law, and family law. Tope’s practice seamlessly blends legal expertise with a deep commitment to social justice, particularly in the areas of child welfare and advocacy.

As the Chair of the Child Rights & Juvenile Justice Center (CRJJC), Tope leads initiatives to provide pro bono legal representation for children in conflict with the law. Under her leadership, the CRJJC has secured the release of juveniles from correctional facilities since August 2022, while advocating for systemic reforms in juvenile justice. Additionally, she serves as Chair of the TOKAN Foundation for Children and Young People, which supports hundreds of children through educational initiatives and partnerships aimed at enhancing child welfare.

Tope’s international experience includes earning an LL.M. in Human Rights and Law & Economic Development from Northeastern University, where she was a Program on Human Rights and the Global Economy Fellow. Her global outlook also extends to her work with clients in Texas and her contributions to international publications on environmental law, trade, and arbitration.

With a proven track record of leadership, advocacy, and innovation, Tope remains committed to building equitable legal systems and empowering vulnerable communities through education, policy reform, and access to justice.

Lavina Sequera is the Co-Founder of Soil of India, a social enterprise supporting over 200 million artisans in India (60% of whom are women). She has also served as a cultural advisor at Triveni Kala Sangam, an art and cultural institution in New Delhi, India.

Sequera is a merit scholarship holder (2022-2023) from the University for Peace - UN Mandated (UPEACE), where she studied International Law and Human Rights. She has over 15 years of experience dedicated to social and humanitarian initiatives across government, private, and non-profit sectors in India. She spearheaded India's largest rural CSR program for Hindustan Unilever Ltd., spanning 70,000 villages from 2010-2012. She also established a women's empowerment and income-generating program across 600+ rural artisans, preserving endangered craftsmanship for Soil of India.

In the past, Sequera has supported humanitarian efforts such as mapping rural Tanzania to combat female genital mutilation (FGM) under the UN's aegis. She has also mediated legal/international aid to sustain the welfare of children in an orphanage in Madhya Pradesh, and volunteered at schools for the blind in Worli, Mumbai and for street children in Mumbai Central.

Sequera is currently a member of the Maharashtra State Women's Council, which runs 10 NGOs in Mumbai. She has been recognized as one of Asia's Top Sustainability Superwomen by CSRWorks International and the Global Reporting Initiative in Singapore. She has also received the Eco-Business A List award for 'Sustainability Leadership during Covid-19' from Eco-Business in partnership with Trucost, part of S&P Global, Singapore. Additionally, she was named one of 'Women for Change 2021' by ChangeNow.

Sequera currently serves as the Honorary Executive Director for Women Empowerment and as the Global Goodwill Ambassador for Human Rights and Peace for India. She is also the Honorary Executive Director of CSR for the National Council of News and Broadcasting, both of which are signatories to the UN Global Compact.

Furthermore, Sequera works with animal activists for emergency response, aid, and activism.

This letter expresses my keen interest in applying for a suitable position in your organization. With relevant education and experience of 14+ years in all aspects of Architectural & Design Direction in the IT industry, I am confident in my ability to deliver value and growth in this position.
Being resourcefully experienced in Micro-architecture for the complex Custom/ASIC products focusing in any one/more areas: High/Low speed peripherals, NPU, Embedded Processors, DSP, Graphics, and/or general-purpose microprocessors, I leverage expertise in managing the RTL design experience, Synthesis, static-timing closure, formal verification, gate-level simulations, and block-level function verification.
In my current role as an Technical Staff Design Engineer with Microchip, India I have developed hands-on experience in various aspects of ASIC development including Micro architecture, design, integration, and synthesis with technical expertise in Micro architecture and design, RTL design, Linting, CDC & RDC, Synthesis, LEC, HLS, FPGA Prototype on hardware development using Xilinx Spartan 6, IP Verification – RTL, HDLs – Verilog, VHDL, System Verilog, Bus interfaces – PCI, AXI, AHB, APB, I2C, ATB, Programming languages – C, C++, System C, Design interfaces – SAS4, SATA, USB3.1, USB 2.0, PIPE, UTMI /UTMI+, OTG 2.0, EHCI 2.0, RGMII, RMII/MII, CSI 2.0, and EDA tools including -

Apart from these, my educational background is complemented by a Bachelor of Engineering- Electrical and Electronics from Madurai Kamaraj University, India.
My resume is enclosed for your consideration. I would appreciate an interview to assess the mutual suitability of the job in detail. Should you have any questions or wish to schedule an interview, I can be reached at +91 810 5233 771 or kannansemi@gmail.com. I positively look forward to speaking with you further and discussing my future contributions to the growth of your company.
Thank you for your time and consideration.

Kannan M

Abubaker Sekatuka is a public health advocate and a project management professional with over six years of experience in project implementation and community engagement in the nonprofit sector. He earned a Bachelor’s degree in Public Health - Health Promotion from Uganda Martyrs University in Uganda and a Diploma in Nursing from Mulago School of Nursing and Midwifery. Over the past six years, Abubaker has advocated for maternal, neonatal and child health rights, sexual and reproductive health, specifically pregnancy care, disease detection and prevention by training community health workers and strengthening Community Health Systems. Currently the moderator of Transparency and Accountability Community of Practice (CoP) of the Community Solutions Program, a U.S Department of State funded training program for grass-roots leaders across the world implemented by the International Research and Exchanges Board (IREX). He has demonstrated the cultivation and nurturing of healthy, inclusive, and thriving safe spaces.

Previously, Abubaker worked as a Community Health Supervisor with Living Goods under the USAID-funded Result Based Financing program. He advanced health education and promoted maternal and child health awareness to prevent the spread of malaria, pneumonia, and diarrhea in remote villages in Uganda. Specifically, he recruited, trained, and mentored four hundred eighty community health workers who graduated and served their communities which reduced under-five year old mortality by 27% in Uganda over a year.  Abubaker has volunteered in several organizations like World Federation of Public Health Associations where he serves on the policy committee by drafting public health policies. He is a certified Human rights consultant from the U.S Institute of Diplomacy and Human rights and a Goldin Global Fellow where he contributes to the Community of Practice and exploring the Asset-Based Community Development model in practice. Through these experiences, he has developed strong program management and engagement skills. With a strong passion for reproductive health and youth development, Abubaker established Sharing Circles, an initiative that combats trauma among the youth through mentorship, creating opportunities and building their power. He also Co-founded Love to Love organization which empowers orphans with love, care, and support in Uganda.

My work experience has aligned with animal rights, veganism, and climate change. In my Campaigner role at The Save Movement, I have enhanced my organizational abilities and cultivated a reputation as a significant contributor through planning, communication, content writing, and management.

 I have also undertaken Social Media training through Sentient Media, an evolving journalistic non-profit focussing on Animal Rights Journalism. I led a team of 10 volunteers from Nepal, Turkey, and India and created a social media strategy and schedule. In the subsequent months, we made content for mass awareness on social media. 

I am enrolled in the first Master's program in Animal Protection Laws in India at the National Academy of Legal Studies and Research, Hyderabad, which includes non-lawyers like me to gain insight into legal paradigms.

Apart from my education and professional exposure, I have always been inclined toward community building and have taken steps on a personal level to implement waste recycling and composting programs at my place of residence and in my college during my bachelor's. In doing so, I have also engaged with waste pickers and traced how unethical and underpaid their jobs are. Apart from that, living near landfills and breathing and drinking in that atmosphere is something nobody should do. Since no stringent policies and steps exist, this is one of the most pressing issues. It is also the starting aspect that moved me towards climate change advocacy. At the same time, I have collaborated with groups working on better education and WASH in these localities in my hometown Delhi. 

I worked at the Climate Save Movement, which aims to sensitize the linkage of animal agriculture and plant-based food systems transitions. Here I lead the Chapter in India. My primary responsibility is to create more awareness by researching how devastating and exploitative industrialized farming systems are towards nonhuman animals and the environment. 
While working here, I also chanced upon building education modules for children, specifically from marginalized communities across India. As a capstone, along with a small team of other inspiring young people, we have worked on a curriculum that is building on the English Language and concepts of Animal Rights and Climate Change for students in Cambodia in association with Veg Voyages Foundation. 

I worked at the Federation of Indian Animal Protection Organisations (FIAPO) as a Social Media Coordinator - handling extensive work from drafting reports on legal matters to social media calendars or overlooking analytics/KPIs.
